title: A canonical numeric string offset addresses the integer array key, so both key guards are reachable

ground_truth.statement: PHP casts an array key that is a canonical decimal integer string to int, so $data['10'] and $data[10] are one element. For [10 => 'kept'], array_key_exists('10', $data) and isset($data['10']) are both true and $data['10'] is 'kept'; neither guard is impossible and neither read is of type never. Non-canonical near misses ('10x', ' 10', '+10', '1.0') stay strings, so the claim is about canonical integers only.

notes: Mago 1.57.0 reports two diagnostics on code that demonstrably runs: impossible-condition on the array_key_exists('10', $data) guard and no-value on the guarded $data['10'] read, because its array-key reconciliation builds a string key where the shape carries the integer key 10. PHPStan 2.3.1 and Psalm 6.20.0 are silent. The runtime script is the neutral ground truth: it shows the string offset reaching the int key in both directions (read and write) and shows the non-canonical controls staying strings, so the guards are reachable and the reads are strings, not never. The pattern was taken from mago/repro/array-shape-numeric-string-key-normalization/repro.php; the comments in that reproducer were treated as a lead, not as evidence, and the fixture here is a clean-room rewrite that only keeps the pattern.
